item.title: Media Relations Coordinator
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 8/28/2026.

The Brookings Institution is a nonprofit public policy organization based in Washington, DC whose mission is to equip decision-makers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies. The Office of Communications works to grow Brookings' impact and effectiveness as a change agent for public policy in the United States and around the world. The Media Relations Coordinator supports the Office of Communications and Public Affairs' earned media efforts by helping connect Brookings research, experts, events, and institutional priorities with relevant audiences across the media ecosystem. Note: this position is included in the staff bargaining unit, Brookings United, affiliated with the IFPTE Local 70 union. Hybrid in Washington, DC (at least two days of remote work each week). 1-3 years of professional experience required. Cover letter and resume required as one document. Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

Key responsibilities include (65% Media Relations Support): monitoring shared media inboxes and supporting the timely routing, tracking, and resolution of media inquiries; coordinating logistics for media interviews, podcast appearances, and other engagements between journalists and Brookings experts; drafting and distributing press releases, media advisories, expert availability notices, and other materials; maintaining and updating media lists, journalist databases, and contact records in Meltwater and other institutional systems; conducting media monitoring and compiling daily, weekly, and ad hoc coverage reports; tracking media placements, interviews, citations, and other earned media activities; researching reporters, editors, producers, podcasters, and other communications channels to support outreach efforts; and assisting in the preparation of media briefing materials for scholars and staff. (20% Communications Support): assisting in developing social media copy, newsletter content, and website updates; supporting communications planning for publications, events, and institutional initiatives; and providing copy-editing, proofreading, and quality-control support. (15% Team Operations and Analytics): maintaining reporting dashboards, tracking tools, and departmental documentation; preparing regular earned media reports and metrics summaries for communications leadership; and coordinating team meetings, training sessions, and schedules.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, public policy, political science, international relations, marketing, or a related field; minimum 1-3 years of professional experience in communications, journalism, media relations, public affairs, public policy, government communications, nonprofit communications, or a related field; strong written, verbal, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills; familiarity with AP Style preferred; exceptional attention to detail; demonstrated ability to organize information, manage data, and maintain accurate records; and proficiency with Microsoft Office applications. Experience with Meltwater or similar media monitoring platforms preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $60,000-$63,000. Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Union (IFPTE Local 70 bargaining unit). Hybrid in Washington, DC. Cover letter and resume required as one document.

Feeding America is the nation's largest charity and the leading domestic hunger-relief charity in the United States, operating a nationwide network of member food banks. The Specialist, Government Affairs supports key government affairs lobbying efforts to increase food, funds, and resources for Feeding America. The position manages resource development in support of Feeding America's legislative and policy priorities and will coordinate across government affairs and policy teams to manage federal nutrition program data collection and analysis. This is a hybrid position based out of Feeding America's Washington, DC office (average 2 days/week in office, with access to a 30-day 'work anywhere' program annually). E-Verify. Salary $88,740-$93,740.

Key responsibilities include: supporting the development of resources for lawmakers utilized by the Government Relations team, network members, Feeding America leadership, external organizations, and policymakers with a focus on SNAP, TEFAP and other commodities, Food is Medicine, and child nutrition; establishing and streamlining systems to house Feeding America resources and regularly update them on internal platforms like Hungernet; operationalizing a process for providing regular reports on Hill engagement in Quorum; supporting annual appropriations work, authorizing campaigns, network fly-ins, and other priorities in close collaboration with Government Relations managers; monitoring emerging news, federal policies, and legislation affecting the Feeding America network of food banks; attending hearings, markups, and partner meetings and providing hearing report-outs and after-action reviews; and drafting newsletter articles and PowerPoint slides for the weekly Government Relations newsletter and monthly network webinars.

Qualifications: strong writing and research skills; basic knowledge or familiarity with Capitol Hill and the legislative process; excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to tailor communications to a variety of audiences; strong project management and critical thinking skills; ability to manage multiple projects and competing deadlines; and strong attention to detail. Experience with MS Office, Quorum, Tableau, Canva, and other legislative tracking platforms preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $88,740-$93,740. Comprehensive Feeding America benefits. Hybrid in Washington, DC (average 2 days/week in office; 30-day 'work anywhere' program annually). E-Verify.

Note: Pacific Legal Foundation (PLF) is a libertarian public interest law firm dedicated to individual liberty, property rights, economic freedom, and limited government. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation's first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to individual liberty, with 18 Supreme Court victories out of 21 cases litigated. The State Policy Analyst will work with PLF's litigation, strategic research, coalitions, and communications teams to develop both model policies and actual legislation that advance liberty and individual rights. The position is fully remote. 1-3 years of legislative drafting experience required. Law degree preferred.

Key responsibilities include: working with PLF litigators and the policy team to draft innovative policy solutions in areas such as anti-discrimination, economic opportunity, challenges to the administrative state, property rights, and energy abundance; conducting legal research to support policy drafting; drafting one-pagers and other supporting documentation for PLF's model policies; reviewing legislation and providing technical support to the state policy team; and occasional travel (approximately 5%).

Qualifications: at least 1-3 years of experience drafting legislation; a law degree or extensive knowledge of the law and public policy strongly preferred; knowledge of and a principled passion for individual liberty consistent with PLF's mission; and proof of strong writing and research skills. Apply via Talent Market with specific materials: resume, cover letter, and two work samples (authored legislation + policy advocacy piece for general audience) as one PDF.

AFC comprises more than 500 elected officials, local leaders, military groups, and businesses that work together to advance resilient and equitable flood solutions at the local, state, and federal levels. The Senior State Policy Associate will join the state and technical policy team, which is responsible for developing and scaling flood resilience policies and best practices between states. The position is based in Washington, DC, hybrid (in-person Tuesdays and Thursdays). No more than 10% travel. Relocation assistance of up to $4,000 available for new employees living outside the DC metropolitan area.

Key responsibilities include: developing state policy recommendations, guidance, and templates by synthesizing insights informed by evaluations of state legislation and state agency proposals, cross-state comparisons of policy and programs, and research on technical flood topics; sharing information, supporting knowledge transfer, and sparking dialogue on flood resilience best practices and policies including planning and facilitating in-person and virtual meetings with senior state leaders such as Chief Resilience Officers and Directors of Departments of Water Resources; and contributing to internal strategy to advance flood resilience in key geographies and advising senior staff on key insights by breaking down strategic questions into clear, actionable steps.

Qualifications: 5+ years of experience in policy research, policy development, or program delivery; applied knowledge in areas such as state legislative and regulatory process, government funding and finance, infrastructure policy, or environmental and water resources policy (e.g., experience in a state legislature, state agency, local government, regional entity, or policy-focused nonprofit); strong track record of communicating complex issues in a clear, credible, and compelling manner for a variety of audiences; demonstrated aptitude in policy development including project management, critical thinking, and strategic communication; and demonstrated experience managing multiple projects and stakeholders simultaneously.

item.title: Rhode Island Policy Advocate
item.description:
Green Energy Consumers Alliance is a nonprofit organization with a mission to empower consumers and communities to speed a just transition to a zero-carbon world, combining consumer-facing programs with public policy advocacy at the state level in Massachusetts and Rhode Island. The Rhode Island Policy Advocate will be a key person on the Advocacy Team, working to influence state-level legislative and regulatory energy policy primarily in Rhode Island. Note: the Advocate must be a registered lobbyist in Rhode Island. The position requires Rhode Island residency and roots in Rhode Island -- meaning residence and familiarity with the geography, politics, and communities. A valid driver's license and proof of COVID-19 vaccination including a booster shot are required. The position title and level will be determined based on the qualifications of the chosen candidate. To apply, send a resume and cover letter to jobs@greenenergyconsumers.org by August 15, 2026.

Key responsibilities include: participating in and representing the organization in all relevant Rhode Island policy discussions, coalitions, advisory bodies, and more; leading coalitions relating to decarbonization as assigned; engaging in advocacy on state legislative efforts and regulatory activity related to energy efficiency, beneficial electrification, renewable energy development, and equitable clean energy and climate policy; lobbying legislative and executive branches on organizational priorities and state climate policy; working some evenings particularly during the legislative session (January-June); nurturing and cultivating strategic partnerships with Rhode Island climate and energy stakeholders; researching and drafting organizational positions on state climate and energy policy; drafting and presenting testimony at public hearings and meetings; assisting with member and prospect communications; supporting organization events; and assisting in grant writing and reports to funders.

Qualifications: a bachelor's or master's degree in environmental or energy studies, public policy, or a related field and relevant work experience; passion for climate action; knowledge and experience with public policies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in transportation, buildings, and electricity sectors; roots in Rhode Island meaning residence and familiarity with the geography, politics, and communities (required); research experience preferably in the energy field; excellent interpersonal, written, and oral communications skills; valid driver's license (required); and proof of COVID-19 vaccination including a booster shot (required).

Compensation and logistics: salary $60,450-$74,100/year ($31-$38/hr for 37.5 hours/week), commensurate with qualifications, experience, and title. Benefits include health, dental, 403(b), short- and long-term disability, 4 weeks paid vacation, and 12 days sick time per year. Hybrid in Providence, RI (at least 1-2 days/week in Providence office). Deadline: August 15, 2026.

item.description:
IMPORTANT: This is an AmeriCorps VISTA service position, not a salaried employment role. VISTAs receive a daily living allowance of $68.39/day (approximately $24,962/yr), not a salary. Applications must be submitted through the AmeriCorps website at https://my.americorps.gov/mp/listing/viewListing.do?fromSearch=true&id=130169 -- do NOT use the IRC careers page Apply button. Service commitment begins September 8, 2026 for 12 months. Application deadline: August 14, 2026.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. The Economic Empowerment VISTA will make meaningful contributions to IRC Denver's Economic Empowerment programs, supporting both near and long-term outcomes of stabilization, poverty reduction, and community integration for refugees and asylees. The position is hybrid in Denver, CO (3 days in-office, 2 days remote).

Member duties include: drafting programmatic policies and procedures for review by IRC staff; researching and assisting in development of frameworks to monitor programs and outcomes; developing resource-mapping systems; designing surveys or other client feedback tools and reviewing client feedback; and conducting research across project areas including employment skills development, financial capabilities, English language learning, technology use support, and navigation of systems for basic needs access. VISTA assignments do not include regular direct service work.

Qualifications: openness to working with people from varied backgrounds; ability to work both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment; and proficiency with Microsoft Office. Must commit to completing 12 months of full-time service beginning September 8, 2026. Must meet all AmeriCorps eligibility requirements.

Compensation and logistics: AmeriCorps daily living allowance $68.39/day. Upon successful completion of service, VISTAs may be eligible to receive a $7,395 education award or $1,800 cash end-of-service stipend. Additional AmeriCorps benefits include health benefits, relocation allowance (if eligible), childcare assistance (if eligible), 10 days personal leave, 10 days sick leave, and parental leave. Hybrid in Denver, CO. 37.5 hours per week. Deadline: August 14, 2026.

item.title: Intelligence Intern – Fall 2026 (Remote)
item.description:
CrowdStrike is a global leader in cybersecurity, on a mission to stop breaches with an AI-native security platform. Its University Recruiting program offers paid positions for students and recent grads. This Intelligence Internship sits within CrowdStrike's Counter Adversary Operations team and involves hands-on experience collecting and analyzing data shared on the cybercriminal underground that could impact the security and privacy of CrowdStrike customers and their users.

Key responsibilities include: supporting a wide variety of data collection activities across multiple source types and collection methods; building and maintaining automated collection pipelines leveraging APIs and web scraping across open and closed sources; configuring and managing collection tooling for reliable data acquisition; and conducting and evaluating open-source research and exploratory data analysis on cybersecurity topics supporting CrowdStrike customers.

Qualifications: currently enrolled in a 4-year university with at least 1-2 years of study remaining after the internship, graduating in 2027 or 2028, working toward a degree in computer science, computer engineering, information security, intelligence studies, cybersecurity, cybersecurity policy, international relations, math, physics, or a related field; proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language such as Python, or analytical languages such as SQL or R; hands-on experience with AI-assisted coding tools; and functional or professional fluency in one or more of Chinese (Mandarin or Cantonese, strongly preferred), Korean (strongly preferred), Spanish (strongly preferred), Arabic, or Farsi. Bonus points for interest in cybersecurity, OSINT tooling knowledge, and command-line tooling.

Compensation and logistics: the hourly rate for U.S. candidates is $28-$35. This is a fully remote, 12-week internship at 10-20 hours per week during standard business hours, running August-November 2026. The expected close date of the posting is August 24, 2026.
